summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of gastroparesis, GJ tube placement, and prior cecal volvulus presented with a two-day history of diffuse abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, consistent with a gastroparesis flare. She had elevated white blood cell count on admission but no signs of infection, and blood and urine cultures were negative. CT imaging showed no bowel obstruction or acute abdominal process. Pain was initially managed with IV morphine, but due to concerns about opioid-induced gastric slowing, she was transitioned to tramadol. Nausea was treated with lorazepam and tube feeds were successfully restarted. Her leukocytosis resolved spontaneously. As part of a planned outpatient procedure, her GJ tube was replaced by interventional radiology during the admission. She improved clinically, tolerated full tube feeds, and was discharged home with instructions to avoid opiates, continue new and home medications, and follow up with her primary care provider.
